source.title: CNNs Avoid the Curse of Dimensionality by Learning on Patches
source.authors: Vamshi C. Madala; S. Chandrasekaran; Jason Bunk

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, though the publication header has placeholder dates and DOI.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on CNN generalization with natural image labels using a patch-based training procedure, a different method from the claim versions. It does not test any version's defining comparison or intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper trains CNNs on patches assigned their parent image labels, then reports patch-averaged accuracies. Table 1 also gives patch-wise training accuracies; these are included with the test accuracies in the same rows. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests its own patch-learning explanation of CNN generalization, but none of V1–V8. It varies patch size and training duration without the random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example comparisons those versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that patch-training results and similar heat maps support CNNs learning patch labels, and that their preliminary theoretical model estimates observed generalization errors reasonably closely. They acknowledge crude approximations and omission of CNN capacity and optimization effects.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains CNNs on image patches labeled with the parent image class and aggregates patch logits at inference; it does not test the listed claim versions' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Patch size and dataset change reported accuracies; ImageNet patch training also reports different results at different epoch counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Patch-trained ResNet18 models attain substantial image-level test accuracy after averaging patch logits. Selected intermediate patch sizes outperform full-image training: 75.0% versus 66.8% on CIFAR-100 and 83.0% versus 70.3% on STL-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training CNNs on patches with parent-image labels and averaging patch logits can generalize to held-out images; performance depends on patch size and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Patch-trained ResNet50 models achieve 66.5%–74.7% ImageNet top-1 accuracy. For 96 × 96 patches, accuracy rises from 70.8% at 100 epochs to 72.4% at 1280 epochs; the cited full-image reference reaches 78.4% at 88 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ImageNet patch training yields substantial accuracy, with performance dependent on patch size and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: SegNeXt trained on 256 × 256 crops reaches 44.7 mIoU after a reported 320k epochs, compared with 48.1 using 512 × 512 images after 160k epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Patch-based semantic segmentation can approach full-image performance under the reported unequal training durations.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing
record.problems: The paper itself notes that its theoretical approximations are preliminary and omit CNN capacity and optimization effects. It reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed empirical accuracies. ImageNet patch results use different epoch counts, and the paper states that a full patch-size sweep could not be done due to resource constraints.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out chance performance, paired with natural-label performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
CNN versus fully connected performance, the contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and their dependence on tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized training examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. Citing Jiang et al. and deriving an input-domain error bound do not test V7's weight-perturbation measure. All Table 1 accuracies are image-level accuracies computed after averaging patch logits, despite the paper's patch-wise terminology. No omitted result bears on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label generalization.
Does not sweep network width or test performance beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks or isolate local connectivity.
Does not compare batch sizes or adapt large-batch recipes.
Does not test dropout or its interaction with data augmentation.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not identify memorized examples, remove them, or compare their removal with random removal.
